news.title: FA chair demands Infantino release World Cup sell-off documents
news.lede: Gianni Infantino was first elected as Fifa president in 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has been told to release all documents relating to his controversial plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup in a letter sent by Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt. Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, said that the Fifa Council should also receive a written explanation for the cancelled suspension of United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup. Infantino should make all documents available before the next Fifa Council meeting, which is on 15 October.

news.title: England World Cup star ruled out of Nations League games as club confirm injury blow
news.lede: The Inter Milan defender has suffered a thigh injury, his club have confirmed. Stones is set to be sidelined for a minimum of three-and-a-half weeks after straining a muscle in his left thigh. However, Inter fear he could be out for up to a month, missing their next four matches in all competitions. At best, the 32-year-old will not return to action until after the upcoming international break.

India has been drawn in Group K for the inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival set to take place at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Baku, Azerbaijan between October 22 and 31. The inaugural edition of the competition will be conducted in a format different to the original rules, featuring an 8v8 format, with two 20-minute halves separated by a five-minute half-time break. The pitch will measure 68 metres by 50 metres, while rolling substitutions will be permitted throughout the match.

news.title: England World Cup star set to miss out on Thomas Tuchel's latest squad after club confirm major injury setback
news.lede: JOHN STONES is set to miss out on Thomas Tuchel’s latest England squad after Inter confirmed the defender has suffered a thigh injury. Three Lions boss Tuchel is due to name his first squad since the World Cup on Friday at 10am, with Stones now facing a race against time to recover from the setback. Inter confirmed on Thursday morning that the 32-year-old has suffered a muscle strain to the flexor muscles in his left thigh. The Italian giants said Stones underwent clinical and diagnostic tests at the Istituto Humanitas in Rozzano, with his condition set to be reassessed over the coming days.

news.title: Reportage - Ukraine reconstruction tool funded by Built World Cup launches
news.lede: A reconstruction tool funded by the proceeds from the 2025 Built World Cup football tournament – which raised £10,000 for Ukrainian architecture practice balbek bureau – has launched and can now be used for the Cherkasy region. RE: Ukraine Villages documents traditional architecture and material-use through in-depth field research to create culturally-sensitive plans and elevations to facilitate reconstruction and preserve a unique sense of place appropriate to the region. The Built World Cup, founded by ING Media and The Developer, is a tournament for mixed-gender built environment teams to raise money for charity. The funds raised by the Built World Cup 2025 were used to visit 42 villages in Cherkasy to document the local vernacular, covering thousands of kilometres to photograph architectural details and collect references.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel can start new England era with 6 call-ups after World Cup autopsy
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel spoke about “ball possession” and the “English DNA” as the fundamental reasons behind their World Cup semi-final defeat. Tuchel was brutally honest about England’s failings after the disappointment in Atlanta and looked for reasons as to why they lost to Argentina. Fans, pundits and journalists rightly seized on his words as he was quizzed about England losing a control of a game they had within their grasp. Why they retreated deeper and why Tuchel made defensive substitutions.

news.title: Capital Football duo set to represent Australia at IFCPF World Cups in Atlanta
news.lede: Two products of Capital Football’s All Abilities program will fly the flag for the ACT this October, with Luc Launder and Carly Salmon named in the CommBank Pararoos and CommBank ParaMatildas squads for the IFCPF World Cups in Atlanta, USA. Launder, a defender, has been selected in the 14-player CommBank Pararoos squad for the IFCPF Men’s World Cup 2026, running from 12 to 24 October. Head Coach Kai Lammert’s side has been drawn into Group B alongside Brazil, Spain and Chile, with all matches to be played at the U.S. Soccer National Training Center.
